name: How it is done
rule: A word that tells HOW something is done usually ends in -ly.
She drives carefully. He spoke softly.

wrong.text: The old man walked slow up the stairs.

right.text: The old man walked slowly up the stairs.

spot: Is the word describing an action (walk, speak, work)? Then it needs the -ly form.
deeper: 'Good' describes a thing; 'well' describes an action: a good singer sings well.
After 'is', 'feels' or 'looks' keep the plain word: the soup smells good.
Some words stay the same: fast, hard, early.
